subject: general
question: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm, at a distance of 6 cm. Its image is formed at a distance of ________ and is_________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**12 cm, virtual.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given problem is related to the reflection of light by a concave mirror.
 
• The focal length of the mirror is given as 12 cm, and the object is placed at a distance of 6 cm from the mirror.
 
• Therefore, the object distance (u) is -6 cm (negative sign denotes that the object is placed in front of the mirror) and **f****ocal length (f) **is **negative** for concave mirror.
 
• To find the image distance (v), we can use the mirror formula: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where f is the focal length of the mirror.
 
• Substituting the given values, we get** v = 12 cm.**
 
• The resulting image is magnified, erect, and** virtual.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A** concave mirror** is a curved mirror in which the inner side of the curved shape is the reflecting surface.
 
• Its surface has an inward curvature that makes it resemble the interior surface of a hollow sphere.
 
• The fact that they **induce light rays to converge**, or gather together after reflection, makes them **converging mirrors** as well.
 
• **Real and virtual image**s can be formed by an object and mirror placed in different positions.
